chunks.text: DRYER GUIDE How to Use the Dryer Whirlpool Model (to confirm) Never dry anything that has ever had gasoline, solvents or any oil on it (including cooking oil), even after washing. No washer can remove all oil. Fire or explosion risk. Items with foam, rubber or plastic: dry on a clothesline or with Air Dry only (no heat).

Never run the dryer if the lint screen is loose, damaged, blocked or missing. Do not reach in while the drum is moving. Do not let children play on or in the dryer. Use the dryer only when you are at home.

1 POWER turns the dryer on and off. The round button chooses the cycle. TEMP sets the heat on timed cycles. CYCLE SIGNAL turns the end beep on or off. STATUS lights show progress. 1 Clean the lint screen before every load: pull it straight up, roll the lint off with your fingers, and push it firmly back in. Do not rinse it to remove lint. From the manufacturer's manual, page 6.

2 Empty pockets. Put the laundry in loosely and shut the door. Do not overload: clothes need room to tumble. 3 If you use a dryer sheet, use only one, put it in at the start (not on a half-dry load), and use it only once.

5 Push the cycle button until the light is on the cycle you want. Automatic cycles (left side) sense when the clothes are dry. Timed cycles (right side) run for 60, 40 or 20 minutes. 6 Press and hold START/PAUSE to begin. For a large load, hold it for 2 to 5 seconds. 1 HEAVY DUTY (hot, about 45 minutes): towels, jeans and other heavy items.

2 NORMAL (warm, about 35 minutes): corduroys, work clothes, sheets. 3 DELICATE (low heat, about 30 minutes): lingerie, blouses, washable woollens. 4 On automatic cycles the heat is set for you and cannot be changed. Times vary with the load size and fabric.

5 Timed cycles (60, 40 or 20 min) are for bulky items, bedspreads and heavy work clothes, or to finish a damp load. They start on Hot: press TEMP until the heat you want (Hot, Warm, Low or Air Dry) lights up. If clothes are still damp at the end, run another timed cycle.

1 Use a timed cycle with Air Dry for foam rubber (pillows, padded bras, stuffed toys) and plastic (shower curtains, tablecloths): about 20 to 30 minutes. Rubber-backed rugs: 40 to 50 minutes. Sheer nylon and olefin: 10 to 20 minutes. 2 Check covers are stitched shut. Stop now and then to shake and fluff pillows. Foam pillows dry slowly: make sure they are completely dry.

1 You can change the cycle or the heat any time before you press START/PAUSE. Three short beeps mean that choice is not possible, and it is ignored. 2 To change the cycle after it has started: press POWER, press POWER again (or the cycle button), choose the new cycle, then press and hold START/PAUSE. The new cycle starts from the beginning.

3 On timed cycles you can change the heat at any time by pressing TEMP. 4 To pause: open the door or press START/PAUSE once. To restart: close the door and press and hold START/PAUSE. 5 To stop at any time: press POWER. 1 The STATUS lights show Wet, Damp, Cool Down and Done. A light inside the drum turns on when you open the door.

2 When Done lights up, take the clothes out straight away so they do not wrinkle. 3 Press CYCLE SIGNAL, before or during a cycle, to turn the end-of-cycle beep on or off. STOP AND CONTACT PROPERTY MANAGEMENT

You smell gas (gas dryers): do not light anything or touch any switch or phone in the building. Leave, call the gas supplier from a neighbour's phone or from outside, or the fire department, then property management. The WET light is flashing with a pause between flashes: the dryer has found a problem that needs service.

The drum turns but there is no heat, or a breaker or fuse for the dryer trips again after you reset it. A burning smell or smoke: press POWER and do not use the dryer again. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
Based on the manufacturer's manual W10296184B for this Whirlpool electronic dryer. Pictures are taken from that manual. Updated 20 October 2026.

Whirlpool Model (to confirm) Never run the dryer if the lint screen is loose, damaged, blocked or missing. It can overheat and damage the dryer and clothes. Keep the area around the dryer clear of lint, dust and anything that blocks the air flow. Never store gasoline or other flammable products near it. Do not take any part of the dryer apart or try to repair it.

1 Clean the lint screen before or after every load. It is in the door opening. Pull it straight up, roll the lint off with your fingers, push it firmly back in. Do not rinse it: wet lint is hard to remove. A blocked screen makes drying slow. 2 If lint falls into the dryer when you take the screen out, tell property management: the vent hood needs checking.

3 Use only one dryer sheet per load, and only once: sheets can block the air grille. Use only softener or anti-static products that say they are safe for dryers. Wash the lint screen every 6 months 1 Do it sooner if the screen looks clogged, if clothes take longer to dry, or if the dryer stops before the load is dry. Detergent and softener leave a coating on it.

2 Roll the lint off with your fingers, then wet both sides of the screen with hot water. 3 Scrub it with a nylon brush, hot water and liquid detergent to remove the build-up. 4 Rinse it with hot water, dry it well with a clean towel, and put it back in the dryer. Clean the drum (when it has stains)

1 Make a paste of powdered laundry detergent and very warm water and put it on a soft cloth. Or use a non-flammable household cleaner. Rub the stains until the dye is gone. 2 Wipe the drum well with a damp cloth, then tumble a load of clean cloths or towels to dry it.

3 Blue jeans and bright cottons can stain the drum. This is harmless and does not stain other clothes. Dry these items inside out to avoid it. Around the dryer and when away 1 Keep the area around the dryer and its exhaust opening free of lint, dust and dirt. Do not pile laundry against it or block the vents in a closet door.

2 Use the dryer only when you are at home. Before a long time away, clean the lint screen and ask property management whether the dryer should be unplugged. STOP AND CONTACT PROPERTY MANAGEMENT The lint inside the dryer cabinet and in the exhaust vent needs removing every 2 years or more often. This must be done by a qualified person.
The light inside the drum does not work (it needs a special 10-watt appliance bulb; the dryer must be unplugged). The lint screen is damaged or missing. The dryer needs to be moved or reconnected.

You smell gas (gas dryers): do not light anything or touch any switch or phone in the building. Leave, call the gas supplier from a neighbour's phone or from outside, or the fire department, then property management. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
Based on the manufacturer's manual W10296184B for this Whirlpool electronic dryer. Pictures are taken from that manual. Updated 20 October 2026.

DRYER GUIDE Dryer Troubleshooting Whirlpool Model (to confirm) Never run the dryer if the lint screen is loose, damaged, blocked or missing. Do not reach in while the drum is moving. Do not open the dryer cabinet or try to repair it. 1 Check the door is firmly closed. 2 Press START/PAUSE firmly. For large loads, press and hold it for 2 to 5 seconds.

3 Check the breakers or fuses for the dryer (there may be two). If one has tripped, reset it once. If it trips again, or you cannot find it, contact property management. The drum turns but there is no heat 1 Check that Air Dry is not lit. Press TEMP to choose Hot, Warm or Low.

2 Electric dryers use two breakers or fuses. If one has tripped the drum can turn with no heat. Reset it once; if it trips again, contact property management. 1 If the WET light flashes with a pause between flashes, the dryer has found a problem that needs service. Stop using it and contact property management. Clothes not drying, take too long, or are too hot

1 Clean the lint screen. Do this before every load. If it looks coated, wash it (see Dryer Care). 2 Check Air Dry was not chosen by mistake. Choose the right heat for the fabric. 3 Dry smaller loads so clothes can tumble freely. 4 Check no dryer sheet is stuck on the grille. Use only one sheet, only once. 5 The room must be warmer than 7°C (45°F) for the dryer to work properly.

6 If the dryer is in a closet, make sure the vents at the top and bottom of the closet door are not blocked. 7 If it is still slow, the exhaust vent may be blocked with lint. Contact property management. Automatic cycle ends too early, or clothes still damp

1 The clothes may not be touching the moisture sensor strips inside the drum. Dry a fuller load (not packed tight), or finish with a timed cycle. If it keeps happening, the dryer may not be level: contact property management.

2 If all automatic loads come out less dry than you like, you can make every automatic cycle dry longer. The dryer must not be running. Press and hold TEMP for at least 6 seconds until it beeps. The STATUS lights show the setting: Wet only = factory setting, Wet + Damp = 15% more drying, Wet + Damp + Cool Down = 30% more drying.

3 Press TEMP again until the setting you want is lit solid, then press START/PAUSE to save it. To leave without saving, press POWER. 1 A thumping sound for the first few minutes after the dryer has not been used for a while is normal. 2 Thumping or shaking during the cycle: the clothes may be knotted or balled up. Separate them and restart.

3 Rattling or clicking: a coin, button or clip may be caught at the front or back edge of the drum. Check the edges. Empty pockets before washing. 4 If it still shakes or vibrates, the dryer may not be level. Contact property management. Lint, stains, wrinkles or smell 1 Lint on clothes: clean the lint screen.

2 Spots on clothes: put dryer sheets in at the start of the cycle, never on a half-dry load. 3 Blue marks on the drum come from jeans. They do not transfer to other clothes. 4 Wrinkled loads: take clothes out as soon as the cycle ends, and dry smaller loads.

5 Smell after painting, staining or varnishing nearby: air out the room. When the smell is gone, rewash and dry the clothes. STOP AND CONTACT PROPERTY MANAGEMENT You smell gas (gas dryers): do not light anything or touch any switch or phone in the building. Leave, call the gas supplier from a neighbour's phone or from outside, or the fire department, then property management.

The WET light is flashing with a pause between flashes: the dryer has found a problem that needs service. The drum turns but there is no heat, or a breaker or fuse for the dryer trips again after you reset it. A burning smell or smoke: press POWER and do not use the dryer again.

Clothes still take too long after you cleaned the lint screen: the exhaust vent may be blocked or need checking. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management. Based on the manufacturer's manual W10296184B for this Whirlpool electronic dryer. Pictures are taken from that manual. Updated 20 October 2026.

For direct-wired dryers: Electrical Shock Hazard Disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating. Failure to do so can result in death or electrical shock. The dryer light automatically turns on inside the dryer drum when you open the door. 1. Disconnect power. 2. Disconnect wiring. 3. Make sure leveling legs are secure in dryer base. 4. Use masking tape to secure dryer door. Reinstalling the dryer

Follow the "Installation Instructions" to locate, level, and connect the dryer. To change the drum light: 1. Unplug dryer or disconnect power. 2. Open the dryer door. Locate the light bulb cover on the back wall of the dryer. Remove the screw located in the lower right corner of the cover. Remove the cover. 3. Turn bulb counterclockwise. Replace the bulb with a 10-watt appliance bulb only. Replace the cover and secure with the screw. 4.

Plug in dryer or reconnect power. TROUBLESHOOTING First try the solutions suggested here and possibly avoid the cost of a service call... For additional recommendations, refer to your Installation Instructions. Dryer will not run Is the dryer door firmly closed? Was the START/PAUSE button firmly pressed? Large loads may require pressing and holding the Start/Pause button for 2-5 seconds.

Has a household fuse blown, or has a circuit breaker tripped? There may be 2 household fuses or circuit breakers for the dryer. Check that both fuses are intact and tight, or that both circuit breakers have not tripped. Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker. If the problem continues, call an electrician. Is the correct power supply available? Electric dryers require 240-volt power supply. Check with a qualified electrician.

Was a regular fuse used? Use a time-delay fuse. Is the clothing knotted or balled up? When balled up, the load will bounce, causing the dryer to vibrate. Separate the load items and restart the dryer. No heat Has a household fuse blown, or has a circuit breaker tripped? The drum may be turning, but you may not have heat. Electric dryers use 2 household fuses or circuit breakers.

Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker. If the problem continues, call an electrician. Dryer displaying error message (WET indicator flashing) WET indicator is flashing: If the WET indicator on the dryer control panel is flashing, with a pause between flashes, the dryer control has detected a problem that requires service. Call for service. Unusualsounds Has the dryer had a period of non-use?

If the dryer hasn't been used for a while, there may be a thumping sound during the first few minutes of operation. Is a coin, button, or paper clip caught between the drum and front or rear of the dryer? Check the front and rear edges of the drum for small objects. Clean out pockets before laundering. Are the four legs installed, and is the dryer level front to back and side to side? The dryer may vibrate if not properly installed. See the

Installation Instructions. Clothes are not drying satisfactorily, drying times are too long, or load is too hot Is the lint screen clogged with lint? Lint screen should be cleaned before each load. Has the Air Dry temperature setting been selected? Select the right temperature for the types of garments being dried. See "Additional Features." Is the load too large and heavy to dry quickly? Separate the load to tumble freely.

Is the exhaust vent or outside exhaust hood clogged with lint, restricting air movement? Run the dryer for 5-10 minutes. Hold your hand under the outside exhaust hood to check air movement. If you do not feel air movement, clean exhaust system of lint or replace exhaust vent with heavy metal or flexible metal vent. See the Installation Instructions.

Are fabric softener sheets blocking the grille? Use only one fabric softener sheet, and use it only once. Is the exhaust vent the correct length? Check that the exhaust vent is not too long or has too many turns. Long venting will increase drying times. See the Installation Instructions. Is the exhaust vent diameter the correct size? Use 4" (102 mm) diameter vent material. Is the dryer located in a room with temperature below 45°F (7°C)?

Proper operation of dryer cycles requires temperatures above 45°F (7°C). Is the dryer located in a closet? Closet doors must have ventilation openings at the top and bottom of the door. The front of the dryer requires a minimum of 1" (25 mm) of airspace, and, for most installations, the rear of the dryer requires 5" (127 mm). See the Installation Instructions. Cycle time too short Is the automatic cycle ending early?

The load may not be contacting the moisture sensor strips. Level the dryer. Lint on load Is the lint screen clogged? Clean lint screen. Check for air movement. Stains on load or drum Was dryer fabric softener properly used? Add dryer fabric softener sheets at the beginning of the cycle. Fabric softener sheets added to a partially dried load can stain your garments.

Drum stains are caused by dyes in clothing (usually blue jeans). These will not transfer to other clothing. Loads are wrinkled Was the load removed from dryer at the end of the cycle? Remove garments promptly to prevent wrinkling. Was the dryer overloaded? Dry smaller loads that can tumble freely. Odors

Have you recently been painting, staining, or varnishing in the area where your dryer is located? If so, ventilate the area. When the odors or fumes are gone from the area, rewash and dry the clothing. IMPORTANT: Your dryness level settings can be adjusted to adapt to different installations, environmental conditions, or personal preference. This change is retained and will affect all of your AUTOMATIC cycles, not just the current cycle/load.

If all your loads on all AUTOMATIC Cycles are consistently not as dry as you would like, you may change the default settings to increase the default dryness level. This change will affect all of your Automatic Cycles. There are 3 drying settings, which are displayed using the WET, DAME and COOL DOWN indicators: STATUS Wet O [ Damp _ [ COO[ Down O

Done 1. (factory preset dryness level) - WET indicator lit. 2. (slightly drier clothes, 15% more drying time) - WET and DAMP indicators lit. 3. (much drier clothes, 30% more drying time) - WET, DAMP, and COOL DOWN indicators lit. To change the AUTOMATIC default settings: NOTE: The AUTOMATIC default settings cannot be changed while the dryer is running. 1. Press and hold the TEMP button for at least 6 seconds.

The dryer will beep, and the current drying mode will be displayed. 2. To select a new drying setting, press the TEMP button again until the desired drying setting is shown. NOTE: While cycling through the settings, the current setting will be lit solid, but the other settings will flash. 3. Press the START/PAUSE button to save the drying setting and exit to standby mode. NOTE: To exit without saving, press the POWER button. 4.
The drying setting you selected will become your new preset drying setting for all AUTOMATIC cycles. 8
